newsitem.title: UK: Gencor aiming bigger and broader - official.
newsitem.headline: Gencor aiming bigger and broader - official.

text.p: Gencor Ltd is betting on a strategy of diversification and acquisition along commodities lines to compete with other top mining houses, a senior company official said on Monday.

"If Gencor is to compete successfully...we are going to have to achieve a critical mass of size, of balance sheet strength, which will allow us to take on board risks associated with international projects," finance director Mick Davis said.
"We have achieved a degree of diversification by commodity and geography and I think that's likely to continue," he said.

Davis was presenting to analysts the company's results for the year ended on June 30. The results, released in Johannesburg last week, showed attributable earnings up to $469 million from $279 million previously.
Exploration for metals and coal was ongoing in Asia, Africa and Australia, with base and minor metals taking precedence over Gencor's roots in the precious metals, Davis said.
Aluminium, the greatest contributor to Gencor's income, is expected to grow still further next year as Gencor had recently acquired 100 percent of the Alusaf aluminium concern, he said.
Gencor also expected its gold and platinum interests to recover following last year's operational setbacks, he added.
The European Union's blockage of a merger between Gencor's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd and Lonrho Plc's platinum interests had been painful, he said.

"The opportunity to really create value has possibly been lost, certainly in this transaction," Davis said, adding that Implats remained an important part of Gencor's portfolio and there were no plans to sell it.
Davis also said Gencor would continue to focus on unlisted investments, which provided the majority of income last year, in order to take advantage of access to cash flows.
